meta.title: Meridian: tools for multilingual teams
meta.description: Meridian is a small studio building quiet, fast tools for teams that publish in several languages at once.

hero.title: Publish once. Read everywhere.
hero.body: We build small, fast tools for teams whose readers do not all speak the same language. No dashboards nobody opens, no per-seat pricing, no watermark on your work.

features.title: What we work on
features.body: Three problems, picked because they are the ones we kept running into ourselves.

items.title: Content that stays in sync
items.body: A translation is only useful while it matches the original. We build the check that tells you when it stopped matching.

items.title: Pages that load at once
items.body: Static output, no framework runtime in the browser, no layout shift. A page should be readable before anyone notices it arrived.

items.title: Tools your team can own
items.body: Plain files in a repository you control, readable by a person and by a machine. Nothing important lives in somebody else's database.

cta.title: Working on something multilingual?
cta.body: We take on two or three projects a year. Tell us what you are building and we will tell you honestly whether we are the right studio for it.

meta.title: About Meridian
meta.description: Who we are, how we work, and the three rules we do not break.

about.title: About the studio
about.lead: Meridian is six people in two cities. We have been building software for multilingual publishers since 2019, and we still write most of it by hand.

sections.title: How we work
sections.body: One project at a time, with the people who will maintain it afterwards in the room. We write the documentation while we build, not after, because the version written afterwards is the one nobody reads.

sections.title: What we believe
sections.body: A tool should be legible. If you cannot open a file and see what it does, you do not own it, whatever the licence says. That is why everything we ship is plain text in a repository you control.

sections.title: Where we are
sections.body: Lisbon and Berlin, five hours of overlap, and an office in neither. We meet in person twice a year, which turns out to be exactly enough.
